previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and esophagitis was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by poor oral intake and vomiting. She was treated in the ICU with an insulin drip, which was transitioned to subcutaneous insulin as her anion gap closed and blood sugars stabilized. Nausea and vomiting improved with antiemetics, and she advanced to a soft diet. A possible UTI was ruled out due to urine contamination, and antibiotics were discontinued. Her home antihypertensives were restarted, and she was switched to pantoprazole for esophagitis. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue her insulin regimen, take pantoprazole daily, and follow up with endocrinology and gastroenterology.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with persistent nausea and 
vomitting and this was felt to be consistent with your prior 
gastroparesis flares.  You were treated with bowel rest, 
antiemetics (antinausea medications), and medications to control 
your high blood pressure. Your symptoms improved while in the 
hospital.  You were seen by the gastroenterology service. 
.

deficiency anemia and to possibly repeat a botox injection at 
that time. You also need to follow up with Dr. ___ 
further management and possible changes in the settings of your 
neuroenteric stimulator.  Please eat small meals and stay 
upright after meals to help with digestion.

physician to discuss your medication management.

help protect your kidneys

nausea
